newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis mostly flat, await PPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - munis mostly flat, await PPI.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds mostly were unchanged in quiet, late trade on Thursday as the market looked ahead to the release of some important economic data that will reveal how retailers and producers are faring.

"It was almost unchanged, with exceptions in two areas. I think the high-grade, intermediate area was slightly easier, just a bit. And my dollar (bonds), I had a difficult time with them. Finally, at the close, I had them unchanged to down one-eighth of a point," a municipal analyst said.

The market, wary that the Federal Reserve again will restrain the economy by raising interest rates, said activity was subdued in part due to the release on Friday morning of the retail sales and producer prices data for March, which will signal just how strong the economy is.

"Tomorrow, we've got a whole series of economic data...So the Treasury and fixed-income markets will give us a guide," a trader said. He explained that participants in the municipal market on Thursday did not seem to have a compelling reason to do deals ahead of those reports.
"It doesn't seem to me that anybody has an axe to grind."

Economists polled by Reuters in a consensus survey look for the Producer Price Index to be flat, though a rise of 0.1 percent was seen when the more volatile food and energy prices were excluded. Retail sales were anticipated at up 0.6 percent overall, and 0.4 percent excluding autos.

Looking ahead on the supply calender, an approximately $920 million sale by John F. Kennedy International Air Terminal Limited Liability Co in New York City, expected during the week of April 21, will be entirely covered by bond insurance if that proves cost-effective, a syndicate official said.
This approach would open the deal up to more institutional as well as retail investors.
A decision will be made shortly, the Lehman Brothers official added.

The host of new issues priced this week--which added up to $4.8 billion, the record for the year so far--appeared to have been cleaned up though a few dealers fretted that their inventories were a bit higher than they would like.
While there were bid-wanted lists being circulated, traders said activity was slower than on Wednesday, adding most of the lists were fairly small. "I didn't see any bangers," one said.
In the secondary market, Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey Revenues of January 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.87 basis point, up one basis point.
North Carolina Medical Care Commission Hospital revenue bonds for Wake County Hospital System of October 2026, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.93 percent, NET, up one basis point.
In the futures market, the June municipal contract rose seven ticks to 112-14/32. The June Treasury bond contract was flat at 107-11/32. The MOB spread was 163 ticks.
